candidates.name: DWH - Global Tourism Project
candidates.what_it_holds: SQL data warehouse built from UN Tourism (UNWTO) statistics: five committed CSV datasets covering domestic tourism, inbound tourism, outbound tourism, tourism industries, and SDG tourism indicators (8.9.1, 8.9.2, 12.b.1), global country coverage, 1995-2022. Repo has Datasets/ (raw CSVs, delimiter-modified for SQL Server), Scripts/ (SQL bronze->silver->gold transforms), Tests/ folders; medallion architecture with star-schema fact/dimension views. MIT licence, last commit ~22 Apr 2026.
candidates.why_useful: A broader, longer-run (1995-2022) global UNWTO panel than what we hold (Eurostat tour_ce_omr is EU-only, 2018-2026). Could give regional tourism-arrivals/expenditure trend context for LatAm/APAC gap (#7) and a cross-check series for global travel demand, though it is a re-shaped mirror of published UNWTO tables, not new primary data.
candidates.size_hint: 5 CSV tables, unspecified row count, SQL DW project

candidates.name: global-tourism-analytics-hayya-morocco
candidates.what_it_holds: Committed UN Tourism / UNWTO outbound-departures Excel file (UN_Tourism_outbound_departures_12_2025.xlsx, dated Dec 2025) covering 1995-2030 (historical + UNWTO forecast horizon), plus a forecasting notebook (_Hayya_Morocco_tourism_Analytics.ipynb) built for the 2030 Hayya Morocco / 2030 World Cup tourism-demand context. MIT licence, updated 16 Apr 2026.
candidates.why_useful: A relatively fresh (Dec 2025 vintage) global outbound-tourism-departures snapshot with a forward path to 2030; could serve as an independent global travel-demand cross-check, and the forecasting methodology (applied to a global mega-event) is a loose analogue for the FIFA World Cup 2026 gap (#11).

candidates.name: tourism-pressure-index
candidates.what_it_holds: Described as "Global tourism built from World Bank, UNWTO, and UNEP data" (a tourism-pressure/overtourism index). README content did not render fully on fetch (likely image/badge-heavy or data pulled live from World Bank/UNWTO/UNEP APIs rather than committed) — needs manual verification of whether source files are committed or pulled at runtime.
candidates.why_useful: If it combines UNWTO arrivals with World Bank population/GDP and UNEP environmental-pressure data into a country panel, it could be a cross-check for regional travel-volume trends (LatAm/APAC gap #7); unverified so flagged low until content is confirmed.

candidates.name: Tourism_Dashboard_PowerBI
candidates.what_it_holds: Power BI dashboard project drawing on UNWTO, World Bank, OECD, and Kaggle tourism data; likely includes an underlying data extract feeding the .pbix file (not independently verified beyond the description).
candidates.why_useful: Possible multi-source tourism panel (UNWTO+World Bank+OECD) bundled for BI use; low confidence without inspecting the .pbix data model.
candidates.size_hint: Power BI file, data extract size unknown

candidates.name: Montecarlo-GBM-Analysis (Jordan Tourism Board passenger demand forecast)
candidates.what_it_holds: Passenger-demand forecasting project for the Jordan Tourism Board using OAG Traffic Analyser data (2012-2025), World Bank WDI, UNWTO, and IMF WEO series; OLS log-log regression, residual-based Monte Carlo and GBM simulation; forecast horizon 2025-2030 (6 years forward, 13 years historical).
candidates.why_useful: A worked example combining airline traffic (OAG) with UNWTO/World Bank/IMF macro series for tourism-demand forecasting — a usable methods template for MIDAS/nowcasting-style work (gap #17) even though the underlying OAG data itself is licensed and likely not redistributed in full.

candidates.name: Tourism-data-analysis
candidates.what_it_holds: Examines international travel and tourism sector growth using a WTTC report as a data source (per repo description); 29 stars, Python/HTML, last updated 2019-05-13 — old but has some traction.
candidates.why_useful: One of the few repos directly citing a WTTC report as its data source; worth checking for a committed WTTC economic-impact extract (GDP/employment contribution by country), which would plug directly into the WTTC gap in this theme, though the repo is stale (2019) so any data would be pre-2019 vintage only.

candidates.name: TourVis
candidates.what_it_holds: University project (TNM048 course) visualizing tourism flows using the UNWTO Tourism database; likely a committed extract of UNWTO bilateral tourism-flow data.
candidates.why_useful: If it contains bilateral tourist-flow matrices (origin-destination), that is a finer-grained dataset than aggregate arrivals counts and could support cross-border-share proxies (gap #20), but it is old (2022) and small.

candidates.name: tourism-satellite-account-analysis-of-Japan-2023
candidates.what_it_holds: Jupyter-notebook analysis of Japan's CY2023 Tourism Satellite Account (likely sourced from Japan's Cabinet Office / JTA TSA release), examining how tourism consumption connects to industry structure, employment and capital formation.
candidates.why_useful: Japan TSA is a genuine national tourism-satellite-account release (APAC gap #7, JNTO angle); this and the near-duplicate RyoKawada repo are small analysis notebooks, not raw data mirrors, so value is mainly as a pointer to the underlying Japan TSA CY2023 release rather than a portable dataset.

candidates.name: Tourism-Satellite-Account-Analysis-of-Japan-CY2023
candidates.what_it_holds: Near-duplicate of the ryokiti0104 repo above (same author pair, same topic): Japan CY2023 Tourism Satellite Account analysis notebook, MIT licensed.
candidates.why_useful: Same as above — pointer to Japan's national TSA release, not independently valuable beyond the first listing.

notes: This theme was hit hard by tooling failures: the shared WebSearch budget was already exhausted (200/200) before any query in this run could execute, so all initial queries returned zero results. html.duckduckgo.com/html/ returned only a CAPTCHA challenge for every query (no usable results). www.bing.com/search returned pages but WebFetch's summarizer could not extract organic web-search results reliably (got unrelated cached/irrelevant content). What worked was (a) `gh search repos` via the CLI, which is rate-limited aggressively (hit 403 'API rate limit exceeded' repeatedly, needed 40-65s waits between retries) but returns clean structured JSON, and (b) WebFetch directly against github.com/search?q=...&type=repositories, which renders GitHub's own search results and was fetchable via WebFetch (subject to its own 429s under load) without needing gh's rate-limited API. Recommend future scouts on GitHub-search modality try github.com/search?q=...&type=repositories via WebFetch FIRST as a DuckDuckGo/Bing substitute when WebSearch budget is exhausted -- it was far more reliable than either search engine's HTML page for this run. Substantive finding: there is no GitHub repository mirroring BEA's Travel and Tourism Satellite Account releases, no WTTC economic-impact dataset mirror beyond one stale 2019 repo, and only fragmented, mostly-notebook UNWTO re-analyses -- the strongest hit is Daniele1388's UNWTO 1995-2022 five-table CSV warehouse. This theme looks genuinely thin on GitHub: WTTC and BEA TSA data are typically consumed directly from their own sites/Excel releases rather than mirrored by developers, so a human may be better served fetching WTTC/BEA source files directly rather than continuing to search GitHub for this theme.
